XMSS is pure hashing, so the chain checks it directly — no oracle, no trusted server. The verifier is a clean-room implementation of RFC 8391, and we say exactly how far its proof reaches: every RFC primitive, and the checks that reject malformed input, are

for all inputs against a line-by-line transcription of the RFC. Composing them into the root comparison that finally accepts or refuses a well-formed signature is argued by hand, checked symbolically at tree height 2, and pinned by RFC vectors at h = 4, 10 and 20.
gas per verification, measured at h = 20
Halmos lemmas checking the verifier against RFC 8391, ten of them for all inputs
XMSS verifier, written from the RFC, no borrowed code
Leaf reuse is impossible by construction

XMSS is stateful: reusing a one-time leaf would let an attacker forge. The Ledger commits its counter before releasing a signature, and the contract keeps a used-leaf bitmap that reverts on any reuse.

Do we have to move our assets or change our Safe?
No. You install a Guard on the Safe you already have. Owners, threshold, history and addresses stay exactly the same.
What happens if the Administrator's Ledger is lost?

Your owners can remove the Guard on their own, with no quantum key, after a 14-day public countdown. If the request isn't legitimate, your owners can cancel it at any point during that time with an ordinary Safe transaction. A lost device can never permanently lock your Safe.
Does this slow down our transfers?
Each transfer needs one extra approval from the Administrator on a Ledger. Batches — like a payroll run of up to 100 transfers — need just one approval for the whole batch.
What does it cost in gas?
Verifying the post-quantum signature costs about 745,000 gas, paid once when an approval is created (745,003 gas measured at h = 20). The check when the transaction executes is a lookup.

Safe v1.3.0 and later. The Safe must have no enabled modules, because modules skip guards — or be on Safe 1.5+ with FermionGuard's module guard installed too. Why XMSS and not ML-DSA or Falcon?

XMSS is a NIST-approved (SP 800-208) hash-based signature, so the EVM can verify it for about 1M gas. Lattice schemes like ML-DSA and Falcon would cost tens of millions of gas to verify on-chain today.
Can we use it in production today?

Not yet. The post-quantum verifier is machine-checked against RFC 8391 as far as described above, and the Guard contracts are implemented and tested, but nothing is audited yet; the Ledger app and Safe App are in development, and an external audit is required before any mainnet deployment.
